title: "External screen" and "Built-in screen" concepts don't apply when only using 2 or more desktop monitors, providing an awkward UX
line: On a desktop with two monitors, the screen layout switcher now treats the primary monitor as the built-in one instead of whichever is listed first.
explanation: OsdAction::applyAction() (used by the Display Configuration applet and the Meta+P OSD) looks for an output of type Panel to call 'built-in'. When there is none, as on a desktop, it fell back to the first output in libkscreen's list, which is ordered by output id and has nothing to do with which screen is primary, so every action hit the wrong screen. Disabling that screen also made the other one primary, so the roles kept swapping. Now, only when no output is a panel, the primary screen is used as the built-in one; it's remembered per pair of monitors in a small state file (~/.local/state/kscreenosdstaterc) while it's turned off, and any action that turns it back on makes it primary again.

commits.message:
osdaction: use the primary screen when there is no built-in one

On desktops with no built-in panel, the layout actions took the output
listed first as built-in, often not the primary one. Now they use the
primary screen, remember it while it's off and make it primary again.

BUG: 522288

media.caption: Two desktop monitors, left one primary: 'Only use built-in screen' turns off the primary screen
Same steps with the fix: the primary screen stays on and the other one is turned off

review.text: Using the primary monitor as the stand-in when no `Panel` output exists, remembering it per monitor pair while disabled, and restoring its primary priority is a good behavioral direction for dual-monitor desktops. However, this patch only fixes the backend behavior while leaving all UI labels saying 'built-in screen' and 'external screen' on desktops, which leaves half of the reported UX problem (and the bug title itself) unresolved and makes closing `BUG: 522288` premature. There are also small logic issues in `osdaction.cpp`: `min_element` on `Output::priority` mishandles unset priority `0`, `NoAction` triggers state writes, disabled outputs get priority `2`, and the existing `osdactions` autotest has no coverage for the new path.
changes: Update `OsdAction::availableActions()` (and its callers in the applet/OSD) to take whether a built-in `Panel` output exists (or the `KScreen::Config`) and use desktop-appropriate wording (e.g. 'Only use primary screen' / 'Only use secondary screen' / 'Extend to left/right of primary screen') when there is no built-in screen.

Use `copy->primaryOutput()` (falling back to `outputs.first()`) instead of `std::ranges::min_element(outputs, {}, &Output::priority)` so an enabled output with unset priority `0` is not chosen over priority `1`.

Return early for `Action::NoAction` before calling `builtInStandIn()` so a no-op does not read/write `kscreenosdstaterc`, and set `external`'s priority to `0` rather than `2` when `!external->isEnabled()` (e.g. in `SwitchToInternal`).

Add unit test cases to the existing `osdactions` autotest covering the no-built-in-panel primary stand-in, persistence across single-screen mode, and primary restoration (with `QStandardPaths::setTestModeEnabled(true)` so tests do not touch real user state).

reviews.text: The behaviour change is right and in the right place. It implements what c7/c8 asked for: on a desktop the primary output stands in for the built-in one, the choice is remembered while it's off, and it's made primary again on re-enable. The laptop (Panel) path is untouched, and the rig steps cover only-built-in, extend both ways, only-external and mirror. But the current title, set by Nate after c4, is about the 'Built-in'/'External' concepts not applying to desktop monitors, and the notes admit the labels are unchanged. On a two-monitor desktop the user still picks 'Only use built-in screen' to mean 'only the primary one', so the awkward UX the title names is still there. Smaller points: writing a state file from OsdAction::applyAction is a side effect that the osdactions autotest now also hits (no QStandardPaths test mode), and the stand-in rules are worth a line in the commit message.
changes: When no output is a Panel, give the actions desktop wording (e.g. 'Only use primary screen' / 'Only use secondary screen', or the monitors' names) by passing the config to availableActions(), in both the applet and the Meta+P OSD; then keep BUG: 522288
Enable QStandardPaths::setTestModeEnabled(true) in the osdactions test, and add a desktop (no Panel) case covering the primary stand-in and the remembered output
Test the Meta+P OSD path too, or state clearly in the MR that only the applet was exercised
